status: Proposed. ADR-002 "Amendment 2026-11-04" (docs/architecture/adr-002-host-broker-trust-contract.md). Nothing reads this file at run time yet; the Broker (PR3, PR4) and the Control Plane client (PR5) will. A value here changes only together with the Amendment.
notes: This file fixes the SHAPE of the new traffic of the production Broker: the requests and replies of the new `_vm` pipe, the two actions the claim pipe learns to claim, and the states a claim reply and an inspect reply may carry. It fixes no behaviour (what the Broker does with a valid request is the Amendment).

limits and enums are the numbers and word sets of the Amendment; test/docs-reversible-approval-contract.test.mjs pins them to the Amendment text and to a reference checker. requestKeys is the exact key set of each `_vm` request body.

vmRequests: `request` (an object the test serializes with JSON.stringify) or `rawRequest` (exact text, for what JSON.stringify cannot write: a duplicate key, a BOM). expected is { ok: true } or { ok: false, reason, field? }. reason is one of: malformed_json (the contract's strict reader refuses it, depth 2), too_large (the frame is over limits.maxRequestBytes; built by the test, not stored), request_shape (the root is not an object with exactly one key naming a known kind whose value is an object), key_set (the body has not exactly the keys of requestKeys[kind]), field (a value is out of range; `field` names it; the first failing field in sorted key order).

vmReplies: `reply` (object) or `rawReply` (text). `kind` is the request kind it answers. For attestTaskStart and attestNetwork `forRequest` names the vmRequests case it answers and `now` is the clock (Unix seconds) the Control Plane checks the statement at. The envelope inside is a real statement signed with an EPHEMERAL ECDSA P-256 key (publicKeySpki below; the private key was discarded after signing, nothing secret is in this file). The Control Plane check is the existing contract: verifyTaskStartAttestation / verifyNetworkAttestation with expected = the request values; a refusal is { reason: "attestation", code, field } with the contract's own code. reason statement_not_enough = a task-start statement whose network is not "none" or whose checkpointType is not "production": the Broker never signs one for attestTaskStart (it answers denied), so one in a reply is refused. reason invariant = restorable is true while state is "restoring".
A refusal is always { "ok": false, "code": "denied" }: the reason is the Broker's log, never the wire.

claimActions: the action DTO (`dto`, or `rawDto` text) of the three-key claim { receipt, signature, action }. The purpose follows from the action: task.start is guest.command, environment.start and environment.restore_checkpoint are broker.operation. expected.ok carries the purpose and the action digest the Broker would recompute (the contract's computeActionDigest). Refusals use the Broker's existing words: action_invalid (does not parse, breaks a contract rule, or the args are not exactly the shape of the action) and action_mismatch (a valid action this form does not claim).

claimReplies: `claim` is first (the claim was just recorded) or replay (an exact duplicate). A first claim always answers UNKNOWN (the claim means "recorded", never "done"); a replay answers the recorded state, which the Broker's worker may since have moved to APPLIED or NOT_APPLIED, and carries "replayed": true (the key is never present with false). inspectReplies: the receipt-less inspect always names synthetic.inspect.
The reply size limits (limits.maxVmReplyBytes, limits.maxClaimReplyBytes) are checked by the test on built frames, not stored as cases.
